buy_title: The stack, one tap each: the two subscriptions the workflow needs, the voice that finishes it, and three cheap things that make the input photo better
buy_total: The software: about $30–$45 a month at the entry tiers seen in September 2026 (a paid Claude plan plus Higgsfield's smallest plan; both change often, so the plan pages show today's). The desk kit: three small Amazon purchases whose buttons show today's prices. The Amazon buttons are paid links: as an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases. The software buttons are ordinary links; we hold no affiliate relationship with Higgsfield, Anthropic or ElevenLabs at the time of writing.

cards.name: Higgsfield (the rendering half: images, video, the MCP connector)
cards.badge: Render · the one subscription that opens every video model
cards.chip: Kling · Veo · Seedance in one app · MCP
cards.price: from $9 to $79 a month at September 2026 prices (plans renamed twice this year; treat any price as a snapshot)
cards.buy_if: you want one subscription that carries the current top video models, a filmmaking layer on top of them, and the official connector that lets Claude drive it.
cards.skip_if: you only ever need one model: Kling direct starts at $10 a month and Google's AI Pro plan includes Veo 3.1 for $19.99, both without a credit balance that expires.
cards.owners: Praise in 2026 reviews: model breadth, speed, the Cinema Studio camera controls, the one-URL MCP setup. Complaints: credits burned on failed generations, prices and plan names that keep changing, a refund policy that covers unused credits only.

buy.pick: The smallest plan is enough to learn on; move up only when the plan step is producing shots you keep. Never buy annual before one month of real use.
buy.check: On the plan page: monthly credits, that unused credits do not roll over, and that MCP generations always spend credits even on plans sold as unlimited. Read the refund terms before paying.
buy.label: See Higgsfield plans

cards.name: Claude (the planning half: shot list, prompts, review)
cards.badge: Plan · the director that never touches a credit
cards.price: free tier for chat; Pro $20 a month; Max from $100 at the time of writing (custom connectors need a paid plan)
cards.buy_if: you want the planning, prompt-writing and review steps done in one conversation, with the connector that sends approved shots to Higgsfield when you say so.
cards.skip_if: you already write shot lists and prompts by hand and just want to paste them into Higgsfield's web app; the free tier is enough to try the planning method.
cards.owners: What the tutorials agree on: the value is the plan step, and a one-line idea sent straight to video wastes credits. Custom connectors work in the web and desktop apps, in Cowork and in Claude Code.

buy.pick: Pro is the practical floor: long conversations, photo uploads, and custom connectors. Max only if you batch dozens of jobs a day.
buy.check: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector; the Higgsfield connector then asks for a Higgsfield login. Set every generating tool to approval-required.
buy.label: See Claude plans

cards.name: ElevenLabs (the voice that turns a silent clip into an ad)
cards.price: free tier (non-commercial, attribution required); Starter about $5–6; Creator about $22 a month at the time of writing
cards.buy_if: your clips need a narrator, a product name pronounced right, or a dubbed version for a second market; the paid tiers carry the commercial licence.
cards.skip_if: the video runs on music and captions only, or you record your own voice; the free tier's licence does not cover a paid ad.
cards.owners: The voice tool named most often in the tutorials we reviewed and in one creator's published pipeline; complaints are about credit maths on long scripts and voices drifting on long passages.

buy.pick: Starter for a few ads a month; Creator when you dub or run more than about ten minutes of speech a month.
buy.check: The commercial licence starts at the paid tiers; free-tier audio must credit elevenlabs.io and cannot be used in a monetised video.
buy.label: See ElevenLabs plans

cards.name: Foldable photo light box, 12–16 inch (with LED strips)
cards.badge: Input · the $30 that fixes half of all bad renders
cards.chip: Foldable · LED · white and black backdrops
cards.price: budget tier; the button shows today's price on Amazon
cards.buy_if: your product photos are shot on a kitchen counter; the models copy every shadow and colour cast they are given.
cards.skip_if: you shoot people or large items, or you already own a softbox.
cards.owners: Praise in owner reviews: even light and the fold-flat case. Complaints: flimsy backdrops on the cheapest boxes, and LEDs that run cool-white only.

buy.pick: A 16-inch box fits a shoebox-sized product; 12-inch is enough for bottles and gadgets.
buy.check: Two LED strips, a white and a black backdrop, and a front shooting hole; "dimmable" if you shoot glossy things.
buy.label: See today's price

cards.name: Phone tripod with a ball head and remote
cards.badge: Input · the same angle for every shot
cards.price: budget tier; the button shows today's price on Amazon
cards.buy_if: you want the reference stills the models start from to share one angle and one height, so a series looks like a series.
cards.skip_if: you already own any tripod with a phone clamp.
cards.owners: Praise: the remote and the height. Complaints: wobble at full extension and clamps that won't hold a phone in a thick case.

buy.pick: Any 50–60 inch tripod with a ball head; the remote matters more than the brand.
buy.check: A clamp that holds a phone in a case, a ball head that locks, and a remote in the box.
buy.label: See today's price

cards.name: Portable SSD, 1–2 TB (USB-C)
cards.price: mid-range; the button shows today's price on Amazon
cards.buy_if: you keep the source stills, every generation and the final cuts; a month of this workflow is tens of gigabytes.
cards.skip_if: you already have a fast drive with room, or you delete generations as you go.
cards.owners: Praise: speed and size. Complaints: heat on long copies, short cables, and counterfeit listings promising impossible capacities for pocket money.

buy.pick: 2 TB if you keep everything; 1 TB if you cull.
buy.check: USB 3.2 Gen 2 or faster, a USB-C cable in the box, and a brand you have heard of; the counterfeits live in the "4 TB for $30" listings.
buy.label: See today's price
